correctness.rationale: The symmetric irreducible Metzler star eigenvalue is simple; its second derivative along a nonzero budget direction is positive unless the diagonal perturbation is scalar. A scalar perturbation is incompatible with Σh_i=0 unless h=0, so the optimizer is unique. Leaf permutations then force equal leaf vaccines. Orthogonally decomposing the star gives m−1 leaf-difference eigenvalues and a 2x2 block whose larger eigenvalue F(x) is strictly dominant. Its derivative F′=(1/m−κ)/2 + (κ+1/m)Δ/[2√(Δ²+4mμ²)] and F″>0. The interior stationary equation solves Δ=μ(κm−1)/√κ and x=(B+mμDκ)/(κm+1); clipping to [0,B] proves the exact all-real parameter allocation and endpoint transitions. Substitution yields the affine interior λ*. Independent NumPy full eigenvalue calculations checked 84 configurations against 61 competing symmetric allocations each; finite tests corroborate the proof only.
